newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to import about 2.5-3.0 mln T quality wheat.
newsitem.headline: Russia to import about 2.5-3.0 mln T quality wheat.

text.p: Russian Agriculure Minister Viktor Khylstun said on Tuesday Russia would import about two million tonnes of maize and soy meal and 2.5-3.0 million tonnes of high quality wheat in 1997.

Asked to break down an earlier estimate on Tuesday that Russia would import 4-5 million tonnes of grain in 1997, he said, "Of that volume, I consider that about two million tonnes will be maize and soy meal and 2.5-3.0 million tonnes will be enrichers for food-quality grain."
Russian grain analyst Andrei Sizov of SovEcon Ltd said that enrichers for food-quality grain meant high quality wheat to be mixed in with low quality wheat to make bread.
Khlystun said after a news conference he was unable to say exactly when buying would take place.

Earlier he said Russia's regional administrators in the north and far east would organise tenders for imports and that the state would not take part in the buying. He also said that Russia would export 6-7 million tonnes from its 1996 crop.

Agriculture officials say it is cheaper for Russia to export grain from the western part of the country and import in the east rather than ship Russian grain across the country at high freight tariffs.
